# The rsk Profile

**Version 0.3** (requirements Draft 0.2). Default Profile_Variant: Ravenscar. Variants: Ravenscar, Jorvik.

The Profile is the rsk counterpart of `pragma Profile (Ravenscar)`: a numbered list of restrictions, each with the guarantee it supports, the enforcement categories that establish it (TS type system, MC macro, LN lint, LK linker or binary check, PO proof obligation, RT run-time monitor; the primary category first), its Ada RM D.13 analogue, the subjects and crates it covers, and the Evidence_Items that demonstrate its enforcement. The verification job checks this document's source against Requirements 1, 2, 4, 27.3, and 57 and regenerates this file.

Retired identifiers: none. Reserved identifiers (inactive in v1, R27.3): PR-37 (Static Task-to-core assignment (every Task, Resource, and Endpoint keeps its build-time core).); PR-38 (Per-core SRP: each core runs its own System_Ceiling and dispatches only its own Tasks.); PR-39 (Cross-core sharing only through Endpoints or a spin-based global resource protocol (MSRP or MrsP).).

## Disallowed crates (PR-35, R1.5)

| Crate | Reason |
|---|---|
| `alloc` | heap allocation after Init (PR-15, NG-06) |
| `cortex-m` | core-peripheral access and interrupt masking outside the Kernel (PR-22) |

| `embassy-time` | relative delays and timers (PR-10, PR-24) |

| `futures` | select and join combinators (PR-11) |
| `panic-halt` | second panic handler (PR-19) |
| `panic-probe` | second panic handler (PR-19) |
| `panic-semihosting` | second panic handler (PR-19) |
| `rtic` | second scheduler and BASEPRI writes outside the Kernel (PR-22) |
| `rtic-monotonics` | relative-delay API (PR-10) |
| `rumpsteak` | std and async receive (R39.1) |
| `std` | general-purpose runtime (NG-05, NG-16) |
| `tokio` | async runtime with std (NG-07) |

## Table 4-1: Ada RM D.13 correspondence (Requirement 4)

Classification as defined in R4.1; Jorvik Profile_Variant markers as defined in R4.2.

| Ada RM D.13 item (Ravenscar) | Kind | Classification | rsk treatment | Cites | Jorvik Profile_Variant |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Task_Dispatching_Policy (FIFO_Within_Priorities) | pragma | Deviation | Fixed-priority preemptive SRP dispatch (Requirement 7). Difference: Eligible equal-priority Jobs start in the NVIC's fixed exception-number order, which the Generator assigns in declaration order (DD-03, the resolution of ORQ-17), not in FIFO order of release. Rationale: The dispatch mechanism of DD-01 lets the interrupt controller arbitrate; emulating FIFO_Within_Priorities would add Kernel work to every Release. The order depends only on Generated_Config and on the release instants (R7.3). Constrained by R29.1. R29.1's hep(i) includes every equal-priority Task, so the Analyzer accounts for interference whatever the order. | R7.1, R7.2, R7.3, R29.1 | Same |
| Locking_Policy (Ceiling_Locking) | pragma | Deviation | PR-05, PR-06, PR-22, Requirement 8 (SRP). Ceilings are computed at build time from the declared accessors (PR-06, R8.7), so no Job locks a Resource whose Ceiling is below the Job's Priority. Difference: A Job may enter a nested Critical_Section on a Resource whose Ceiling is below that of an enclosing Critical_Section, which Ceiling_Locking treats as a ceiling violation that raises Program_Error [RN-42]. Rationale: On one core R8.1 keeps the System_Ceiling at the maximum held Ceiling, as RTIC's BASEPRI_MAX lock does [RN-07]. Constrained by R8.3, R8.4, R8.5. | PR-05, PR-06, PR-22, R8.7 | Same |
| Detect_Blocking | pragma | Enforced | PR-08 (static rejection at build time instead of run-time detection). | PR-08 | Same |
| No_Abort_Statements | restriction | Deviation | PR-02: the Application has no operation that aborts a Task. Difference: A Health_Monitor action can end a Job before it reaches its Release_Point (R4.7): END_JOB ends the running Job; RESTART_PARTITION and STOP_PARTITION end every Job of the Partition; SAFE_STATE stops every Release. Rationale: Fault containment and temporal partitioning between Partitions (Requirements 14 and 18). Constrained by R14.9, R18.4. | PR-02, R14.5, R14.9, R18.4 | Same |
| No_Dynamic_Attachment | restriction | Enforced | PR-23. | PR-23 | Same |
| No_Dynamic_CPU_Assignment | restriction | Enforced | PR-04. | PR-04 | Same |
| No_Dynamic_Priorities | restriction | Enforced | PR-03. | PR-03 | Same |

Difference: The Kernel nevertheless monitors every Job against its Budget for temporal partitioning (Requirement 18), with costs bounded by Delta_timer, Delta_detect, and Delta_enforce (Table 13-1) and included in every WCRT (R29.3, R29.4). Rationale: Temporal partitioning (Requirement 18). Constrained by R29.3, R29.4. | PR-24, PR-27, R18, R29.3, R29.4 | Same |
| No_Dependence => Ada.Execution_Time.Timers | restriction | Deviation | PR-24: the Application creates no timers and has no operation to arm an execution-time timer; Budgets are fixed in the App_Declaration (PR-27). Difference: The Kernel uses Budget timers internally and monitors every Job against its Budget (Requirement 18), with costs bounded by Delta_timer, Delta_detect, and Delta_enforce (Table 13-1) and included in every WCRT (R29.3, R29.4). Rationale: Temporal partitioning (Requirement 18). Constrained by R29.3, R29.4. | PR-24, PR-27, R18, R29.3, R29.4 | Same |
| No_Dependence => Ada.Synchronous_Barriers | restriction | Enforced | PR-12. | PR-12 | Kept (deviation) (PR-12): Jorvik removes it; rsk provides no construct that releases a group of Tasks together once a declared number of them are waiting: bounded release state with no multi-task release (PR-12's guarantee). |
| No_Dependence => Ada.Task_Attributes | restriction | Enforced | PR-25. | PR-25 | Same |
| No_Dependence => System.Multiprocessors.Dispatching_Domains | restriction | Enforced | PR-04, NG-02: static core assignment, matching D.13's advice of fully partitioned multiprocessor dispatching [RN-01]. | PR-04 | Same |

## Core_Subset (PR-21, Requirement 57)

The allow-list of `core` items that the Kernel and Applications may use, with the certification evidence that covers each item or the rsk evidence that substitutes for it (R57.5). Scope `kernel-unsafe` means the item is permitted only inside the Kernel_Unsafe_Module.

| Item | Scope | Certification evidence | Substitute rsk evidence | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `core::primitive` | kernel, kernel-unsafe, application | Ferrocene core subset (assumed; confirm against the 26.05 Safety Manual, ORQ-24) |  | bool, u8, u16, u32, u64, usize, i32, i64, f32 (FPU-using Tasks only, PR-31), arrays, slices, references, tuples, unit. |
| `core::marker::{Copy, Sized, Send, Sync, PhantomData}` | kernel, kernel-unsafe, application | Ferrocene core subset (assumed; confirm against the 26.05 Safety Manual, ORQ-24) |  | Send and Sync carry the data-race-freedom argument of PR-05 (R43.3). |
| `core::clone::Clone` | kernel, application | Ferrocene core subset (assumed; confirm against the 26.05 Safety Manual, ORQ-24) |  |  |
| `core::default::Default` | kernel, application | Ferrocene core subset (assumed; confirm against the 26.05 Safety Manual, ORQ-24) |  |  |
| `core::cmp::{PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Ordering, min, max}` | kernel, application | Ferrocene core subset (assumed; confirm against the 26.05 Safety Manual, ORQ-24) |  |  |
| `core::ops::{Add, Sub, Mul, Div, Rem, BitAnd, BitOr, BitXor, Shl, Shr, Not, Index, IndexMut, Range, RangeInclusive, Deref, DerefMut, FnOnce, FnMut, Fn}` | kernel, application | Ferrocene core subset (assumed; confirm against the 26.05 Safety Manual, ORQ-24) |  | Integer operators on the primitive types; overflow is excluded by proof in the Kernel (R44.1) and by the App_Prover in level A and B Partitions (R46.3). |
| `core::convert::{From, Into, TryFrom, TryInto, AsRef, AsMut}` | kernel, application | Ferrocene core subset (assumed; confirm against the 26.05 Safety Manual, ORQ-24) |  |  |
| `core::option::Option` | kernel, kernel-unsafe, application | Ferrocene core subset (assumed; confirm against the 26.05 Safety Manual, ORQ-24) |  | Including is_some, is_none, map, unwrap_or, and pattern matching; `unwrap` and `expect` are excluded in the Kernel (PR-19). |
| `core::result::Result` | kernel, kernel-unsafe, application | Ferrocene core subset (assumed; confirm against the 26.05 Safety Manual, ORQ-24) |  | `unwrap` and `expect` are excluded in the Kernel (PR-19). |
| `core::num::{checked_add, checked_sub, checked_mul, checked_div, wrapping_add, wrapping_sub, wrapping_mul, saturating_add, saturating_sub, MAX, MIN, BITS, to_le_bytes, from_le_bytes, leading_zeros, trailing_zeros, count_ones}` | kernel, kernel-unsafe, application | Ferrocene core subset (assumed; confirm against the 26.05 Safety Manual, ORQ-24) |  | Inherent integer methods used by the time base, the ceiling map, and the Config_Checker-visible tables. |
| `core::num::NonZeroU8` | kernel, application | none | rsk Verus proofs of every construction site (R44.1); used for Task and Partition identifiers that are never zero. |  |
| `core::slice::{len, is_empty, get, get_mut, iter, iter_mut, split_at, copy_from_slice, fill}` | kernel, kernel-unsafe, application | Ferrocene core subset (assumed; confirm against the 26.05 Safety Manual, ORQ-24) |  | Indexing with `[i]` is permitted only where the index is proven in range (Kernel) or checked (Application); the Link_Checker reports panic paths from Kernel entry points (R14.1). |
| `core::array::{from_fn, map}` | kernel, application | none | Kani harnesses over the generated tables (R45.2); Verus specifications of `vstd::array` cover `[T; N]` indexing in the Kernel logic. |  |
| `core::iter::{Iterator, IntoIterator, Enumerate, Take, Rev, Zip}` | kernel, application | Ferrocene core subset (assumed; confirm against the 26.05 Safety Manual, ORQ-24) |  | Only over slices, arrays, and integer ranges, so that every loop has a bound derivable from compile-time constants or a Loop_Bound_Annotation (PR-16). |
| `core::mem::{size_of, align_of, replace, take, swap}` | kernel, kernel-unsafe, application | Ferrocene core subset (assumed; confirm against the 26.05 Safety Manual, ORQ-24) |  |  |
| `core::ptr::{read_volatile, write_volatile, addr_of, addr_of_mut, null, null_mut, NonNull}` | kernel-unsafe | Ferrocene core subset (assumed; confirm against the 26.05 Safety Manual, ORQ-24) |  | Memory-mapped register access; every use carries a justification identifier (R6.4) linked to a Kani harness with a Hardware_Model stub (R45.4). |
| `core::cell::{Cell, UnsafeCell}` | kernel-unsafe | Ferrocene core subset (assumed; confirm against the 26.05 Safety Manual, ORQ-24) |  | `ResourceCell<T>` wraps `UnsafeCell`; its `unsafe impl Sync` cites the mutual-exclusion proof (R8.3). |
| `core::sync::atomic::{AtomicU32, AtomicBool, Ordering, compiler_fence}` | kernel-unsafe | none | Kani harnesses (sequential checking only; R45.6) and the single-core precondition of every Kernel proof (R27.4); used only for the event-log overflow counter and the Init completion flag. |  |
| `core::arch::asm` | kernel-unsafe | none | Each inline-assembly sequence is replaced by a Hardware_Model stub under Kani (R45.4) and validated by an HIL differential test (R49.3); its justification identifier links to the stub's harness or to a recorded review (R6.4). |  |
| `core::hint::spin_loop` | kernel-unsafe | none | Recorded review: a hint with no architectural effect on Armv7-M (`yield`), used only in the idle activity. |  |
| `core::panic::PanicInfo` | kernel-unsafe | none | The single `#[panic_handler]` of rsk-entry (R14.1) uses only `location()`; formatting machinery is excluded (no `core::fmt` in the Core_Subset), which the Link_Checker's symbol check enforces (R57.3). |  |
| `core::prelude::v1::{derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Default), cfg, inline, must_use, repr}` | kernel, kernel-unsafe, application | Ferrocene core subset (assumed; confirm against the 26.05 Safety Manual, ORQ-24) |  | `derive(Debug)` and `core::fmt` are excluded from Flight_Builds: no formatting machinery reaches the binary (R57.3). |
| `core::{assert!, debug_assert!, unreachable!}` | application | Ferrocene core subset (assumed; confirm against the 26.05 Safety Manual, ORQ-24) |  | Excluded from the Kernel: Kernel code reaches no panic path (R14.1, Property 21); in level A and B Partitions the App_Prover shows every assertion holds (R46.3). |

## Change log (R1.6)

### Version 0.3 (2026-10-08)

Content hash: `sha256:eb3e65422996d44833a51aa5e5039ecd68a535158073fba8227d6217027f4e05`

- **Table 4-1 row Task_Dispatching_Policy**: Restated per R4.6 with the resolved equal-priority start order of DD-03 (NVIC exception-number order assigned in declaration order); the row stays classified Deviation because the order is not FIFO_Within_Priorities. Rationale: design.md records the resolution of ORQ-17 (DD-03). Affects: R4.3, R4.6, R7.3.
- **Reserved identifiers PR-37 to PR-39**: Added as inactive identifiers for static Task-to-core assignment, per-core SRP, and cross-core sharing only through Endpoints or MSRP/MrsP. Rationale: R27.3 requires the reservation in v1. Affects: R27.3.
- **Disallowed-crate list**: Made explicit as the [disallowed_crates] table, one reason per crate. Rationale: R1.5 and PR-35 require the list to be part of the Profile. Affects: R1.5, PR-35.
- **Every restriction**: Added subjects, crate coverage, Evidence_Item names per enforcement category, and the RT assumption or reason. Rationale: R1.2, R1.3, R2.2, and R2.3 require them. Affects: R1.2, R1.3, R2.2, R2.3.

### Version 0.2 (2026-10-07)

Content hash: `unavailable (the version predates the machine-readable source)`

- **PR-20**: Each justification identifier links to a proof, lemma, or harness where one is feasible, and otherwise to a recorded review that states why; `unsafe fn` named explicitly. Rationale: design.md Requirements Impact item 5 (decided during task 1.2). Affects: R6.4, R45.1.
- **PR-20, Kernel_Unsafe_Module**: The Kernel consists of rsk-kernel and rsk-entry; the Kernel_Unsafe_Module includes the entry crate (vector table and reset entry only). Rationale: design.md Requirements Impact item 2 (DD-11). Affects: R6.1, R6.3.
- **Ceiling of Endpoint buffers**: The Kernel-reserved level at which Endpoint operations execute is recorded as the buffer's Ceiling. Rationale: design.md Requirements Impact item 1 (DD-09). Affects: R40.1.
